source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Allen campus spans three facilities and publishes 77 MW of IT capacity, making it the second-largest published data center campus in Texas by power. At a typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, 77 MW of IT load translates roughly to 1,925 racks; this is an assumption about utilization and workload, not a claim by the operator. The campus holds certifications for payment card compliance, healthcare data, information security, federal systems, and audit reporting, qualifying it to serve regulated workloads in those domains.

The Allen campus represents 16 percent of all published capacity in Texas, concentrated in a single operator across three contiguous facility codes in the Dallas-Fort Worth region. Texas has 133 mapped data center facilities overall, but only 19 publish power figures, so this campus's 77 MW is visible in a state market that is substantially unmeasured.

The facility does not publish total power consumption, PUE, grid interconnection capacity, water usage, or power source composition. These omissions prevent assessment of whether the campus is constrained by grid supply, cooling resources, or fuel mix. AI scaling impact depends on factors beyond the IT load figure: the campus cannot be read as an enabler or constraint on regional GPU deployment without grid-level and operator-level data not provided here.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
